paras.title: The idea and the survey
paras.text: When Daniel Morris suggested converting an unused room at Greenfield's central bus station into a small library, the proposal was met with considerable doubt. The station was noisy, and previous attempts to make it more welcoming had attracted little public interest. Nevertheless, Daniel questioned the assumption that residents were simply unwilling to read. A survey of 250 people supported his view: although nearly 60 percent expressed a desire to read more frequently, many claimed they lacked the time. Interestingly, these same residents reported spending an average of 25 minutes a day waiting for public transportation.
anchors: the proposal was met with considerable doubt
nearly 60 percent expressed a desire to read more frequently
an average of 25 minutes a day waiting
paras.explain: הכותב מציג ספק ביחס לרעיון, ואז סתירה לכאורה: אנשים רוצים לקרוא, אבל טוענים שאין להם זמן. זמן ההמתנה היומי מסביר מדוע דווקא תחנת האוטובוס עשויה להתאים.

paras.title: Conditional approval
paras.text: Despite these findings, the local council was reluctant to approve the proposal. Some members feared that books would be stolen or damaged, while others doubted whether volunteers could maintain the library without professional assistance. Rather than ignoring these objections, Daniel recommended a six-month trial funded mainly through donations. The council eventually agreed, on the condition that the project's results would be evaluated before any additional support was considered.
anchors: on the condition that the project's results would be evaluated
paras.explain: המועצה לא השתכנעה לגמרי. היא מאפשרת ניסיון זמני ותבחן תוצאות לפני תמיכה נוספת. ההבדל בין אישור מלא לאישור מותנה הוא המפתח.

paras.title: Numbers are not proof
paras.text: The library opened with 300 books, which passengers could borrow without registering, leaving a deposit, or providing identification. Within three months, more than 700 books had been borrowed, and approximately 85 percent were returned within four weeks. Although these results initially appeared encouraging, they raised an important question about how success should be measured. Several council members argued that borrowing figures alone could not establish whether the project had actually increased reading.
anchors: more than 700 books had been borrowed
approximately 85 percent were returned within four weeks
borrowing figures alone could not establish
paras.explain: 700 השאלות הן לא בהכרח 700 תלמידים או קוראים. 85% חזרה בתוך ארבעה שבועות אינה הוכחה שאנשים קראו. צריך להפריד בין השתתפות בפעילות לבין השגת המטרה.

paras.title: A different kind of success
paras.text: A follow-up survey produced a less straightforward picture. While about half of the regular visitors reported reading more frequently, others admitted that they mainly used the library as a place to meet people or escape the noise of the station. Daniel maintained that this unexpected development should not be regarded as a failure. He argued that the value of a public space could extend beyond its original purpose. Nevertheless, practical difficulties remained: rain damaged several books, and residents criticized the limited selection of titles in other languages. Volunteers addressed both problems but discovered that obtaining donated books was easier than ensuring that the collection reflected the community's needs.
anchors: about half of the regular visitors reported reading more frequently
the value of a public space could extend beyond its original purpose
obtaining donated books was easier than ensuring
paras.explain: שני קווי טיעון: התועלת החברתית החדשה היא הצלחה בפני עצמה, אבל גם כמות גדולה של תרומות אינה מבטיחה שהספרים מתאימים לקוראים.

paras.title: What makes it work?
paras.text: A year later, two neighboring towns announced plans to establish similar libraries. Although Daniel welcomed their interest, he cautioned against assuming that reproducing the original design would lead to equally successful results. In his view, the project's most significant achievement depended neither on its modest budget nor on the number of books available, but on the willingness of residents to take responsibility for a shared space. Ultimately, the experiment suggested that meaningful improvements in public life may require a change in attitudes rather than substantial financial investment.
anchors: reproducing the original design would lead to equally successful results
neither on its modest budget nor on the number of books
willingness of residents to take responsibility
paras.explain: המסר: אי אפשר להבטיח הצלחה באמצעות העתקת החדר או קניית עוד ספרים. הצלחה תלויה בנכונות להשתתף ובצרכים המקומיים.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the information given in paragraph I?
options: To explain why earlier attempts to improve the station had failed.
To present the circumstances that made the proposal seem unlikely to succeed.
To show that the station's main problem was its limited space.
To suggest that passengers were becoming less interested in reading.
questions.evidence: the proposal was met with considerable doubt ... previous attempts ... had attracted little public interest.
questions.model: b — The information establishes why Daniel's proposal initially appeared unlikely to succeed.
trap: a: Previous attempts are mentioned, but their exact reasons for failure are not explained.
c: Limited space is not identified as the station's problem.
d: The survey suggests interest in reading, not declining interest.
questions.heTrap: מלכודת המטרה: פרטים אמיתיים מהפסקה אינם בהכרח מטרת הפסקה.
questions.rubric: 10 points only for the correct option.

questions.he: איזה שני ממצאים בסקר מצדיקים ספרייה בתחנה?
questions.stem: Explain how TWO findings from the first survey supported the proposal.
questions.evidence: nearly 60 percent expressed a desire to read more ... many claimed they lacked the time ... average of 25 minutes a day waiting
questions.model: Many residents wanted to read more but said they lacked time. They also spent about 25 minutes a day waiting for buses, which created a chance to read.
trap: Incomplete: '60% wanted to read' — does not explain the time problem.
Wrong: '250 people supported the idea' — 250 is the sample size, not the number of supporters.
Wrong: 'People already read for 25 minutes' — they WAITED, not read.
questions.heTrap: מלכודת שני הרכיבים: 60% + מחסור בזמן; 25 דקות המתנה + אפשרות לקרוא.
questions.rubric: 5 points: desire to read despite lack of time. 5 points: existing daily waiting time can be used for reading.

questions.he: מה מגלה אישור לשישה חודשים על עמדת המועצה?
questions.stem: What does the council's decision to approve only a six-month trial suggest about its attitude? Support your answer with information from paragraph II.
questions.evidence: reluctant ... six-month trial ... on the condition that the project's results would be evaluated
questions.model: The council remained cautious and uncertain. It wanted to evaluate the six-month trial before offering any further support.
trap: Wrong: 'The council fully supported Daniel' — approval was conditional.
Incomplete: 'It was a six-month trial' — reports the fact but does not interpret the attitude.
Wrong: 'The council rejected the proposal' — it approved a trial.
questions.heTrap: מלכודת שינוי עמדה: אישור מוגבל אינו הבעת אמון מלאה.
questions.rubric: 5 points: caution or doubt. 5 points: specific evidence about trial and review before further support.

questions.he: איך אותם מספרים מאפשרים שתי מסקנות שונות?
questions.stem: Explain why the borrowing figures in paragraph III could support TWO different conclusions about the project's success.
questions.evidence: more than 700 books had been borrowed ... 85 percent were returned ... borrowing figures alone could not establish whether ... increased reading
questions.model: The figures suggest that the library attracted borrowers and books were returned. However, they do not prove that people read the books or started reading more.
trap: Wrong: '700 people read books' — 700 loans are not 700 people.
Wrong: '85% read their books' — 85% refers to return within four weeks.
Incomplete: 'The statistics were good' — does not state the negative/limited inference.
questions.heTrap: מלכודת נתון–מסקנה: השאלה דורשת פרשנות חיובית והסתייגות, לא רק ציטוט מספרים.
questions.rubric: 5 points: participation/return figures suggest success. 5 points: figures cannot establish actual increase in reading.

questions.he: למה הממצא שלא כולם קוראים יותר עדיין מעודד?
questions.stem: Why did Daniel consider the follow-up survey encouraging, even though it did not fully support the original purpose of the project?
questions.evidence: others ... used the library as a place to meet people ... value of a public space could extend beyond its original purpose
questions.model: Not everyone read more, but the library brought people together and made the station more welcoming. Daniel valued this social benefit even though it was not the original goal.
trap: Wrong: 'Everyone read more' — only about half reported reading more.
Wrong: 'The original goal was abandoned' — additional value does not erase the original goal.
Incomplete: 'People met friends' — explain why Daniel viewed it positively.
questions.heTrap: מלכודת מטרה מול תוצאה: צריך לציין גם תועלת חברתית וגם את ההערכה של דניאל.
questions.rubric: 5 points: unexpected social benefit. 5 points: it can count as success beyond encouraging reading.

questions.he: מה ההבדל בין השגת תרומות להתאמה לצרכים?
questions.stem: What did the volunteers discover about the difficulty of improving the collection? Answer according to paragraph IV.
questions.evidence: obtaining donated books was easier than ensuring that the collection reflected the community's needs
questions.model: They found it easier to collect donated books than to find books suitable for the people who used the library, including books in other languages.
trap: Wrong focus: 'Rain damaged the books' — true elsewhere, but not the lesson about the collection.
Incomplete: 'They needed more books' — quantity alone is not the point.
Wrong: 'Nobody donated books' — donations were easier to obtain.
questions.heTrap: מלכודת מענה לשאלה אחרת: גשם הוא פרט אמיתי, אבל השאלה על איכות והתאמת האוסף.
questions.rubric: 10 points: explains the comparison. 7: suitability only. 5: language shortage without the broader point.

questions.he: מהו המסר המרכזי של המאמר כולו?
questions.stem: Which conclusion is best supported by the text as a whole?
options: The value of a community project may depend on both practical achievements and local needs.
Successful local projects should be copied only when sufficient financial support is available.
Community projects should give greater importance to social interaction than to their original goals.
Projects that depend on volunteers are usually more successful than those managed by public authorities.
questions.evidence: the willingness of residents to take responsibility for a shared space ... change in attitudes rather than substantial financial investment
questions.model: a — A project succeeds through practical results and the extent to which it responds to its community's needs.
trap: b: Overstates the importance of money; Daniel explicitly stresses people over budget.
c: The text values social interaction but does not say it must always outrank original goals.
d: The text never compares all volunteer projects with all publicly managed projects.
questions.heTrap: מלכודת הכללה: תשובה שלמה צריכה לכסות את הטקסט ולא לקבוע כלל שלא נכתב.
questions.rubric: 10 points only for the correct option.

definitions: a result of an action or decision
a detailed examination of information or a situation
a typical quality of a person or thing
vocabulary.trap: consequence ≠ chance (תוצאה לעומת הזדמנות). critic הוא אדם שמבקר; analysis הוא תהליך של ניתוח.

definitions: having many parts and difficult to understand
large or important in amount or degree
happening or existing at the present time
vocabulary.trap: current ≠ common (עכשווי לעומת נפוץ). considerable מתאר היקף משמעותי, לא רמה מתקדמת.

definitions: to stop something from happening
to make something smaller or less in amount
to suggest that someone should do or use something
vocabulary.trap: prevent = למנוע; decrease = להפחית. recommend = להמליץ; emphasize = להדגיש.

definitions: a set of rules or principles used by an organization
the reason for doing something
all the people living in a particular area
vocabulary.trap: purpose ≠ priority; population ≠ pollution; policy ≠ profession.

definitions: producing the result that was wanted
able to be trusted or depended on
connected to the subject being discussed
vocabulary.trap: effective = משיג את התוצאה הרצויה; efficient = משיג אותה עם מעט זמן או משאבים. reliable ≠ relevant.
